official.description_text:
Postdoc in quantitative characterisation of multivalent binding
Login and apply
School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health at KTH
Job description
We are looking for a postdoc to develop new methods for measuring multivalent binding — the mechanism by which antibodies and many modern therapeutics engage several targets at once. Standard binding assays capture this poorly, which limits how well the behaviour of such molecules can be predicted.
The project combines DNA nanotechnology with amplification- and sequencing-based readouts. You will use programmable DNA nanostructures to present targets at controlled nanometre spacings, and develop assays that quantify how binders engage them. The work is method development with applications in mind, carried out together with the experimental and computational members of the group at the Department of Gene Technology, KTH/SciLifeLab
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Documented experience of quantitative molecular biology methods, such as qPCR, digital PCR or DNA sequencing.
Very good command of English, spoken and written, as this is the working language of the research group.
As a person you are independent and used to driving a research project forward on your own initiative. The work takes place in an interdisciplinary environment, which calls for good collaborative skills and the ability to communicate results clearly. We prefer that you are aware of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline.
Experience of DNA nanotechnology or other forms of programmable molecular self-assembly.
Experience of characterising molecular binding interactions, for example using surface-based or biophysical methods.
Ability to combine experimental work with quantitative data analysis or modelling.·
Experience of supervising students or teaching at university level.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in method development for quantitative measurement of multivalent molecular binding using DNA nanotechnology and sequencing-based readouts, combining programmable DNA nanostructures with amplification and sequencing assays at KTH/SciLifeLab.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position core is molecular biology, DNA nanotechnology, and quantitative characterization of binding interactions—bench-level molecular methods development. Researcher's domain is human-centred HCI, immersive learning, and spatial collaboration. No thematic connection. Position is fundamentally a method-development exercise in molecular/structural biology, not an application or human-centred research context.

methodological_fit.rationale: Researcher has quantitative research and experimental design skills. Position values 'ability to combine experimental work with quantitative data analysis.' However, required expertise is molecular biology (qPCR, digital PCR, DNA sequencing, DNA nanotechnology, binding characterization)—none of which researcher possesses. Quantitative mindset alone is insufficient for domain-specific method development work. No practical methodological overlap.

growth_value.rationale: Position offers no advancement toward stated capabilities in human-centred XR, collaborative immersive systems, or spatial cognition. DNA nanotechnology, molecular binding assays, and sequencing methods are entirely orthogonal to researcher's target identity. No long-term capability gaps addressed.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong institution; SciLifeLab is internationally recognized. However, postdoc in molecular biology does not position researcher for subsequent entry into human-centred HCI or immersive systems research. Two-year postdoc in molecular characterization would create a research profile in structural biology, making re-entry to HCI/XR communities more difficult and requiring substantial re-training.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress). Position requires 'doctoral degree or equivalent foreign degree' completed before employment decision. Researcher must complete and defend thesis; MSc by Research in HCI/XR is not equivalent to PhD in molecular biology or chemistry for postdoc eligibility.

Posting prefers doctoral degree obtained 'within the last three years prior to application deadline.' If researcher completes MSc in 2026 and applies for 2026 postdoc, the degree would not meet this timeline criterion.
risks: Researcher is significantly under-qualified for postdoc position. Background is in HCI and immersive systems, not molecular biology or chemistry. Position requires documented, substantial experience in quantitative molecular biology methods (qPCR, digital PCR, DNA sequencing), which researcher does not possess.
Two-year postdoc commitment to molecular nanotechnology method development creates research profile misalignment with long-term identity and target institutions.
No publications or project work in DNA nanotechnology, molecular binding, or sequencing-based assays; recruitment would likely prioritize candidates with direct bench experience.
Postdoc is explicitly 'method development'—not a research question-driven position. Does not align with researcher's HCI/research-question-driven background.
Security clearance ambiguity (Swedish Protective Security Act) adds potential administrative burden.
